info.title: yourclerk API
info.description:
Hosted identity service built stage by stage. Since Stage 4 it is **multi-tenant**: every end user belongs to an *application*, and each application has its own users, sessions, signing keys, issuer and settings.

**Three kinds of caller, three credentials** (use the green *Authorize* button for the first two):

| Who | Credential | Endpoints |
|---|---|---|
| A developer in the dashboard | `Authorization: Bearer dvt_...` (from `POST /v1/platform/login`) | `/v1/platform/...` |
| A developer's backend | `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...` (secret key) | `/v1/backend/...` |
| An application's end users | `X-Publishable-Key: pk_live_...` header + a session cookie | `/v1/signup`, `/v1/login`, `/v1/me`, ... |

**Quick start in this page**
1. `POST /v1/platform/signup`, then `POST /v1/platform/login`. Copy the `token`, click *Authorize* and paste it under **developerToken**.
2. `POST /v1/platform/applications` with a name. The response shows the **secret key once**; copy it. Note the `publishable_key` and `issuer`.
3. Click *Authorize* again and paste the publishable key under **publishableKey** and the secret key under **secretKey**.
4. As an end user: `POST /v1/signup` and `POST /v1/login`. The server sets an `HttpOnly` cookie named `session_<part of the publishable key>`, which your browser sends by itself. Then try `GET /v1/me`, `GET /v1/sessions` and `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/token`.
5. As the developer's backend: `GET /v1/backend/users` lists that application's users.

**Try the isolation**: create a second application, sign up the same email there with another password, and switch the publishable key. Each application sees only its own users. A token minted by one application fails verification against the other (different issuer, audience and keys), and a publishable key is refused on every secret-key endpoint.

This page only works on the same origin as the API, and the `Secure` cookie flag is off only when `APP_ENV=development`.

post.description: Creates a user **in the application the publishable key belongs to**. The email is trimmed and lower-cased and is unique per application, so the same address can exist in two applications with different passwords. Passwords must be 8 to 128 characters and are stored only as Argon2id hashes.

delete.description: Revokes one of your own sessions; your other sessions stay alive. Someone else's session, an already-revoked one and a malformed id all return the same 404.

post.description: Returns an ES256-signed JWT valid for 60 seconds with claims `iss` (this application's issuer), `sub` (user id), `sid` (session id), `aud` (the application id), `exp`, `nbf`, `iat` and `jti`, signed with **this application's** key. Only the current session can mint tokens, so use the `id` from `GET /v1/me`. After the session is revoked no new tokens are issued, and the last one dies within 60 seconds.

error.message: A valid publishable key is required in the X-Publishable-Key header

get.description: Public, no credentials. Each application has its own key set, and its tokens' `iss` is this URL's `.../apps/{app_id}`. Verifiers fetch the set once, cache it, and check signatures locally. A rotated-in key is listed 10 minutes before it signs anything, and a retired key stays listed for 24 hours. Responses are cacheable for 5 minutes.
Returns only users of the application the secret key belongs to, newest first. A publishable key, a developer token or no credential gets 401.
A user of another application is a 404, exactly like a user that does not exist.

Generates the publishable key, the **secret key (shown only in this response)**, and the application's first signing key. Settings start at their defaults; change them with `PATCH`.

patch.description: Session lifetime and idle timeout apply to sessions created or checked from now on. Try `signup_enabled: false`, then `POST /v1/signup` with that application's publishable key.

post.description: Issues a new secret key, shown only in this response. The old one stops working immediately.

200.description: Application with the new secret key

post.summary: Rotate the application's token signing key
post.description: Two-phase and safe: the new key is published in the JWKS now and signs from `active_from` (10 minutes later); the old key keeps signing until then and stays published for 24 hours. Other applications are unaffected.

publishableKey.name: X-Publishable-Key
publishableKey.description: `pk_live_...` Identifies the application. Safe to ship in a browser; it grants no access by itself.

cookieAuth.name: session
cookieAuth.description: Set by `POST /v1/login` as `session_<part of the publishable key>`. Your browser sends it automatically; you cannot paste it here.

secretKey.description: `sk_live_...` Authorises a developer's server for one application. Never put it in a browser.

developerToken.description: `dvt_...` returned by `POST /v1/platform/login`. Valid for 7 days or until logout.

SessionID.name: id
SessionID.description: Session id (UUID), as returned by `GET /v1/me` or `GET /v1/sessions`.

AppNotFound.description: No such application, or it belongs to another developer

current.description: True for the session making this request

secret_key_last4.description: Last four characters of the active secret key, to tell keys apart

issuer.description: The `iss` of this application's tokens. Configure the SDK with it.

jwks_url.description: Where this application's public signing keys are published

secret_key.description: Present ONLY in the response that creates or rolls the key. It is stored as a hash and cannot be shown again.

allowed_origins.description: Browser origins allowed to call the API. Stored now; enforced with CORS in Stage 8.

session_lifetime_seconds.description: Absolute lifetime of a session, whatever the activity.

session_idle_timeout_seconds.description: A session with no activity for this long is signed out. Cannot exceed the lifetime.

signup_enabled.description: When false, `POST /v1/signup` returns 403 `signup_disabled`. Existing users can still log in.

ApplicationPatch.description: Every field is optional; omitted fields are unchanged.

allowed_origins.description: `scheme://host[:port]`, http or https only, no path or wildcard. Normalised and de-duplicated.
